summary: WebSocket-driven PTY and filesystem control channel on installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs a long-lived client that connects to a WebSocket server (SERVER_URL / config-file value) and dispatches inbound messages through a router in connection/message-router.js. Handlers include terminal_create and terminal_input, which call pty.spawn(shell,...) in terminal.js and write server-supplied bytes directly into the spawned PTY, giving the remote peer an interactive shell on the operator's host. The same router exposes server-initiated write_file, delete_files, move_files, copy, git_commit/git_push, execute (arbitrary conversation execution), and update_llm_config / MCP configuration mutation against the installer's workdir and configuration. Authentication is a shared-secret handshake; once completed, any party controlling the configured server URL has broad remote-control over the machine running the agent. The package is presented as a remote worker agent, but the effect on the host is a persistent externally-driven RCE and filesystem-mutation channel rather than an operator-typed session. service/linux.js modifies PATH (~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin) as part of install; a bundled msal-browser.min.js contains normal Microsoft auth code (ping references are inside standard MSAL logic).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
